title: console: the metadata-admin-only spec validation leaves the first screen (lazy-loaded), the console-side payback of the objectui#11088 D1 ceiling raise
body:
Unblocked: #11073 closed (PR #11086 merged); see `5903794882`.

Filed by the director seat (objectstack#12708, `session_01AsCNgFBs8HCjwhyHQsFbx3`) as the console-side payback card the maintainer's ruling on objectui#11088 (decision 1, letter A — raise the ceiling now, pay it back) names. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Why

PR objectui#11086 (the `@objectstack/*` 17.5.0 bump) raises the console first-screen ceiling by 413.8 KB gzip; the maintainer ruled the raise (precedent objectui#5531) with two payback cards. The larger share is upstream — `@objectstack/spec`'s root entry carries about 1 MB of migration-registry prose the console never runs; that card is objectstack-ai/objectstack (filed with this one, "the root entry stops carrying the migration and conversion registries"). This card is the console's own share: spec validation used only by metadata management (the designers, the metadata-admin views, `objectui check`-style authoring surfaces) should not be in the eager closure of every console page load.

## What this card asks

1. **Measure first.** Which `@objectstack/spec` entries the console's eager closure imports today, and from which routes (the Bundle Analysis comment on PR objectui#11086, `5888891615`, and `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` are the instruments). Name the metadata-admin-only imports and their gzip weight.
2. **Lazy-load them by route** (dynamic import at the metadata-admin / designer boundary), the mainstream shape (an admin surface split from the runtime shell), without moving what the runtime shell needs at first paint.
3. **Lower the ceiling back** together with the headroom assertion, in the same commit as the payback lands, by the amount recovered — the ceiling raise is a loan, not a new baseline.

## Acceptance

- The eager closure measured before and after, in the PR body; the ceiling and headroom assertion lowered by the recovered amount.
- No first-paint regression for the runtime shell; the designers still validate exactly as before once opened.

Related: objectui#11088 (the ruling), objectui#11073 / PR objectui#11086, objectui#5468 (the ceiling stays as shipped unless the maintainer rules), objectui#5531 (the precedent), the upstream card in objectstack-ai/objectstack.
